claims.text: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr is assumed to be a homogeneous, fully recrystallized, single-phase BCC solid solution in the baseline state.
The multielement HfNbTaTiZr alloy exhibits sluggish atomic diffusion.
The multielement HfNbTaTiZr alloy exhibits severe lattice distortion.
The random distribution of five refractory elements in the BCC lattice creates significant lattice distortion.
Lattice distortion impedes dislocation motion in HfNbTaTiZr.
Lattice distortion impedes atomic diffusion in HfNbTaTiZr.
Impeded dislocation motion and atomic diffusion stabilize the alloy microstructure at elevated temperatures.
Solid-solution stabilization and suppressed dislocation mobility reduce high-temperature softening.
Solid-solution stabilization and suppressed dislocation mobility reduce thermal expansion relative to pure constituent metals.
HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit a slower decrease in yield strength with increasing temperature than pure Nb, Ta, Ti, Zr, and Hf.
HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit a slower decrease in elastic modulus with increasing temperature than pure Nb, Ta, Ti, Zr, and Hf.
At 1000°C, the yield strength of HfNbTaTiZr will decrease by less than 30% from its room-temperature value.
At 1000°C, the elastic modulus of HfNbTaTiZr will decrease by less than 30% from its room-temperature value.
At 1000°C, the yield strength of the pure-metal comparators will decrease by more than 50% from room-temperature values.
At 1000°C, the elastic modulus of the pure-metal comparators will decrease by more than 50% from room-temperature values.
The thermal expansion coefficient of HfNbTaTiZr will be 10–20% lower than the average coefficient of its constituent elements.
HfNbTaTiZr stress–strain curves will show less pronounced softening than those of the pure-metal comparators.
HfNbTaTiZr stress–strain curves will show more gradual yielding than those of the pure-metal comparators.
The predicted behavior is expected to hold up to 1200°C at strain rates from 10^-4 to 10^-2 s^-1 for fully recrystallized, single-phase HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed behavior may cease to apply if secondary phases form or at extreme strain rates.
